title: To the Spirit of Spring
text:
And I said when spring arrived,

Do not go on hidden in the colored trees,

Sweetly shake your head

with the foam of flowering seas.


And you rose from the depths of the grass

that whispered with the wind and wept,

saying that you should let the icy seas pass,

seeking your petals that still slept.


And I forgot the motionless foam and sand,

indolent with the brightness of the hours

among the mute trees. And, hand upon hand,

strangely, among the flowers we sang.
editorial_note: The translation follows the Spanish text's spring invocation and keeps its sea-and-flower imagery.

title: Prayer
text:
I turn the corner of prayer and burn

in a blessing of sudden sun

in the name of the condemned

I would turn back or run

to the hidden earth

but the sounding sun

purifies

the sky

Someone

finds me

Oh let him

scorch and drown me

inside his earthly wound

His lightning answers my cry

my voice burns in his hand

now I am lost in the One who blinds

and at the end of prayer the sun's clamor is heard

Version by Elizabeth Azcona Cranwell
editorial_note: The source title does not match the visible body, which is a Spanish version of 'Prayer'; the translator credit is preserved as a final line.

title: This Bread I Break Was Once Oats
text:
This bread I break was once oats,

this wine in a foreign tree

dived into its fruit;

by day the man and by night the wind

reaped the harvests, broke the grape's joy.


Once, in this wine, the blood of summer

beat in the flesh that clothed the vine,

one day in this bread

the oats in the wind were joy,

man broke the sun, struck down the wind.


This flesh you break, this blood you let

sow desolation among the veins

were oats and grape,

born of sensual root and sap;

my wine that you drink, the bread that you snatch from me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sacramental transformation of grain, grape, flesh, and blood present in the Spanish text.

title: Little Drop, My Pain
text:
Little drop, my pain.

I threw it into the sea.

Into the deep sea.

Then I said to myself: To your liking

you may now sail!


But my little faith undid me...

The little faith

of my singing.

Between wave and sky I was shipwrecked.


And the sea was an immense pain.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the miniature pain cast into the sea and returning as immensity.
